The core insight is that pass and run effectiveness are governed by temporal metrics—time-to-throw (t_throw) and time-to-LOS (t_LOS)—which define the operational window for OL\/DL interaction. These metrics are embedded in a dual system: one for pass protection (t_throw) and one for run support (t_LOS and RYOE). The GSI Bayesian framework uses these as sufficient statistics to compute pass-protection likelihood, while GSE employs them to model state transitions in response to blitzes or injuries. The failure mode occurs when t_throw exceeds 3.0s or RYOE falls below -0.5 yards, indicating breakdown in either pass or run leverage. This duality is encoded in the trench temporal leverage primitive, which forms the kernel for both systems. The pocket integrity index (PII) is derived from the active status of the defensive front and t_throw, serving as a scalar proxy for pocket stability. The offensive line engagement model (E_OL) integrates injury and blitz data into a single metric that governs strategic adaptation. All three primitives are defined over a shared temporal domain and map through isomorphisms to GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s reactive planning.
